quotes.text: C++ is a horrible language. It's made more horrible by the fact that a lot of substandard programmers use it, to the point where it's much much easier to generate total and utter crap with it.
quotes.author: Linus Torvalds

quotes.text: There are only two kinds of languages: the ones people complain about and the ones nobody uses.
quotes.author: Bjarne Stroustrup
quotes.source: The Design and Evolution of C++

quotes.text: A language that doesn't affect the way you think about programming, is not worth knowing.
quotes.author: Alan Perlis

quotes.text: Any application that can be written in JavaScript, will eventually be written in JavaScript.
quotes.author: Jeff Atwood

quotes.text: Docker: because 'it works on my machine' wasn't a good enough answer, so now we ship the machine.
quotes.author: Unknown

quotes.text: No matter what problem you post on the internet, someone will suggest rewriting it in Rust.
quotes.author: Unknown

quotes.text: We pointed AI coding agents at WPT and asked them to fill in missing functionality. They made lots of small fixes, and those added up.
quotes.author: Ladybird Team
quotes.source: Hacker News — Ladybird Is Now in Alpha (via simonw)
quotes.extraction_note: Pithy real-world observation on how agents actually help: not magic, just a flood of tiny fixes that compound. Good antidote to both AI hype and AI doom.

quotes.text: Windows is great at the NT kernel — performance, drivers, security model — but Win32 and the UI layer above it is just mediocre. Linux is great at the tools — 'everything is a file', composable command-line programs. Therefore the reverse of this project might be the best outcome.
quotes.author: londons_explore
quotes.source: Hacker News — Win4wine – Run Windows Shell as the Linux Desktop on Wine
quotes.extraction_note: Sharp layered take: keep the good bottom of each stack, throw away the mediocre top. Slightly spicy because it implies both platforms are half-built.
